item.title: Modi Vows Chip Plants, Nuclear Reactors in India Growth Push
item.description: India’s Prime Minister Narendra Modi said the country would build more semiconductor plants and expand its fleet of nuclear reactors, as he reiterated his government’s resolve to make India a developed nation in the next two decades.

item.title: US, Canada Still See Sticking Points Before Deadline for 50% Tariffs
item.description: Canada’s chief trade negotiator told a government advisory group that there’s still a significant amount of work to do to reach an agreement that would stave off a new wave of US tariffs next week.

item.title: Singapore Stocks’ Record Run Gets ‘Goldilocks’ Boost From Growth
item.description: Singapore’s stocks have outperformed the world over the past month as their traditional strengths of high dividend yields and resilient balance sheets get a lift from a “Goldilocks” economic backdrop.

item.title: Bally’s Warns of Going Concern Doubt as It Seeks Fresh Liquidity
item.description: Bally’s Corp. warned investors of “substantial doubt” that it will be able to continue as a going concern as it risks running afoul of its agreement with lenders.

item.title: Lula’s Lead Over Bolsonaro Narrows in Brazil Election Poll
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s lead over right-wing challenger Flávio Bolsonaro narrowed ahead of Brazil’s October presidential election, according to a new poll published Friday.

item.title: Nvidia Has $21 Billion SpaceX Stake, $30 Billion in Intel Shares
item.description: Nvidia Corp. on Friday disclosed a nearly $21 billion stake in Elon Musk’s SpaceX and a $30 billion one in Intel Corp.

item.title: Anthropic Revenue Ahead of IPO Surges Over 14-Fold in Second Quarter
item.description: Anthropic PBC is telling prospective investors its second-quarter revenue jumped at least 14-fold versus the same period a year ago, according to documents seen by Bloomberg News.

item.title: Amazon’s New User Agreement Seeks to Curb Class-Action Suits
item.description: Amazon.com Inc. reintroduced a clause in its user agreement that seeks to prevent shoppers from filing class-action lawsuits against the online retailer, inserting a legal buffer between itself and plaintiffs attorneys that it removed five years ago.

item.title: Berkshire Pads Delta, Alphabet Stakes as Abel Taps Cash Pile
item.description: Berkshire Hathaway Inc. increased its holdings in Delta Air Lines Inc. and Google parent Alphabet Inc. as Greg Abel began tapping into the company’s massive cash hoard.

item.title: Hedge Funds Halved Short Bets on Yen Since Joint Intervention
item.description: Hedge funds further dialed back on their wagers against the yen, signaling a reduction in negative sentiment surrounding the currency after the US and Japan’s historic joint intervention.

item.title: Leveraged ETFs Snap Back as Casino Crowd Mints $50 Billion
item.description: Three weeks ago, Wall Street’s casino crowd took a beating. AI stocks buckled, semiconductor shares tumbled and leveraged trades unraveled.

item.title: Codelco Overhauls Management Team as New CEO Seeks Turnaround
item.description: Codelco is overhauling management and splitting oversight of its operations into northern and central-southern units as new Chief Executive Officer Jorge Gómez seeks to stabilize mines and finances at one of the world’s largest copper producers.

item.title: UK Issues Emergency Phone Alert as Heat Raises Wildfire Risk
item.description: The UK government issued a wildfire alert to mobile phones on Friday as drought and the tail end of a heat wave left much of the country at very high fire risk.

item.title: The Equity and Credit Disconnect Is Getting Really Big Again
item.description: Are stocks missing something?

item.title: Gas Pipeline for Proposed Oracle Data Center Delayed to 2027
item.description: A key New Mexico natural gas pipeline project that would supply power-generation systems for a planned Oracle Corp. data center has been delayed by nearly six months.

item.title: Braskem Optimistic on Talks With Creditors as Deadline Looms
item.description: Braskem SA said negotiations with creditors are advancing as part of an effort to restructure the troubled petrochemicals producer’s finances.

item.title: Fed’s Goolsbee Wants to See More Evidence of Cooling Inflation
item.description: Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago President Austan Goolsbee said he’s encouraged by a recent cooling in inflation but wants to see more of the same in coming months to be sure it’s falling back to the central bank’s 2% target.

item.title: Canada Must Remove Retaliation to Avoid New Tariffs, Greer Says
item.description: Canada needs to scrap its retaliatory trade measures against US products to avoid new tariffs from the White House that are set to take effect next week, US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said.

item.title: ‘Monkey Island’ Creator Finds Wealthy Investor for ‘Thimbleweed Park 2’
item.description: Ron Gilbert didn’t want to go with a traditional publisher for ‘Thimbleweed Park 2,’ so he took an unorthodox route

item.title: Election Angst Fuels Bruising Week in Brazil Markets
item.description: Brazilian assets posted some of the biggest losses in the world this week amid growing angst over the October presidential election.

item.title: Trump Family-Tied Dronemakers (UMAC, PUSA) Get a Boost From New US Tariffs
item.description: Drone makers and suppliers, including two companies with ties to the Trump family, rallied Friday after the White House said it’s applying a tariff on imports of unmanned aircraft systems and their components.

item.title: Bonds Become ‘Really Difficult to Trade’ as Correlations Unwind
item.description: Bond traders face a welter of confusion as fixed-income markets respond more to geopolitical risk and inflation rather than taking cues from traditional signals like US economic growth, according to AlphaSimplex Group’s Kathryn Kaminski.

item.title: GTC Investor May Sell Stake to Break With Hungary Central Bank
item.description: Optima Befektetési Zrt. is considering selling its controlling stake in Globe Trade Centre SA, a move that would end the controversial influence of Hungary’s central bank over one of eastern Europe’s biggest property developers.

item.title: Kushner’s Thrive Capital Invests $215 Million in Amazon
item.description: Joshua Kushner’s Thrive Capital has bought up roughly $215 million worth of shares in Amazon.com Inc., building on the venture firm’s push to invest in public companies.

item.title: Picky Investors Push Back on High-Grade Prices After Debt Deluge
item.description: Blue-chip firms are swarming the US debt market to finance everything from acquisitions to the artificial intelligence buildout. But investors are getting pickier about what they’ll buy, and at what price, as the borrowing frenzy takes its toll.

item.title: Carlyle, CVC Team Up to Bid for Security Systems Group Bauwatch
item.description: Carlyle Group Inc. and CVC Capital Partners Plc are exploring a joint takeover of security systems provider Bauwatch, people familiar with the matter said.

item.title: Airbus Finds System Faults on Air India Jet During Mid-Air Drop
item.description: Airbus SE discovered hydraulic system faults on an Air India Ltd. jet that dropped about 300 feet in mid-flight last week, according to a preliminary assessment by the planemaker.

item.title: Bessent Asked to Justify Yen Intervention in Letter from Warren
item.description: Senator Elizabeth Warren pressed Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent to explain the Trump administration’s justification for intervening in the yen, extending the senior Democrat’s pattern of scrutinizing the Trump administration’s foreign-exchange policies.

item.title: UK Starts Process to Ease EV Mandate in Boon for Carmakers
item.description: The UK will look at watering down its zero-emission vehicle sales mandate, a win for automakers that have been pushing new Prime Minister Andy Burnham to bring forward a review of the targets.

item.title: Colombia Bond Market Perks Up After De la Espriella’s Election
item.description: Colombia’s local corporate bond sales are rebounding after four years in the doldrums as the election of a market-friendly government stokes investor demand for local assets and triggers a drop in sovereign yields.
